2|title: History of Stickyickistan
3|---
4|Stickyickistan is an island on the planet of [[Mythmos]] that is enshrouded in magic, and has one of the largest economies of all the realms. Their economy is based on the cultivation, and export of a wondrous magical plant called [[Arcannabis]], and . The size of the island and how far away it is from other land masses is mysterious at best. Even the most sophisticated magic and technology isn't capable of measuring distance within a certain distance of the island. This area is a Bermuda Triangle like place with its own micro-climate where pilots, and sailors have reported extreme magical weather events, and terrifying creatures from above and below. The presence of such large amounts of [[Arcanite]] beneath [[Mount Zooka]] has warped the fabric of time, space, and the weave itself around the island which is what causes these phenomenon. This makes it incredibly hard to produce a map of the whole island, as the coastlines are enigmatic at best. It can be seen from the [[Lumytholarispace]] , so it does appear on maps of Mythmos, but appears much smaller than going there would lead you to believe.
5|
6|![[Stickyickistan.jpg]]
7|# Modern Stickyickistan
8|
9|Welcome to the enchanting realm of Stickyickistan, a City State where an active volcano stands proudly at its core. This bustling metropolis, inhabited by approximately 27 million denizens, thrives as a tightly woven tapestry of terraced dwellings. At the heart of it all lies the Capitol building, perched upon [[Nevercough Island]], an idyllic smaller landmass embraced by an inlet on the main island. The island experiences tropical weather patterns, with most days in the city being very hot and high in humidity. There are some arid areas of the island further inland where some levels of desertification have taken hold over the years after [[Human Colonialism]] and industrialization.
10|
11|Ascending from the base of the volcano, the upscale residences extend into the lush jungle, offering breathtaking vistas that stretch out to the majestic ocean. The colossal canopy of tropical trees, reminiscent of gargantuan redwoods, provides a natural shield, safeguarding inhabitants from the perilous potential of volcanic eruptions. In stark contrast, the slums that cling to the mountainside exude an aroma of brimstone and sulfur, perpetually shrouded in an ethereal haze of ash and smoke, reminiscent of the favelas of Brazil. These settlements wind their way upward, nearly reaching the rim of the crater in certain areas. Above the slums, an industrial district clings to the rim and delves deeper into the crater, thriving amidst the volcanic terrain.
12|
13|The centerpiece of this mesmerizing landscape, affectionately known to the locals as [[Mount Zooka]], is a unique marvel—a type of volcano called an [[Arcanite]] Cone. These particular cones rise above rich Arcanite deposits, their imposing forms resembling vast mounds of ebony volcanic rock. Near the base, dark, sluggish lava courses through the terrain, surrounding the volcano, while at its zenith, a massive crater brims with bubbling magma. During eruptions, projectiles ranging from golf ball-sized to soccer ball-sized volcanic rocks, globules of molten magma, and occasionally, chunks of Arcanite, burst forth from the crater. After each eruption, the valuable ores, minerals, and particularly the Arcanite, are harvested from the crater. Arcanite, a raw magical element typically found deep within the earth, can be extracted and purified, granting magical properties to weapons and armor. To facilitate this process, the government of Stickyickistan, aka the [[Nevercough Tribunal]], has established makeshift mines and outposts within and around the crater, providing shelter for workers during their resource-gathering shifts.
14|
15|The island's soil boasts copious amounts of nutrients, enriched by high traces of Arcanite. Consequently, the surrounding flora and fauna flourish with extraordinary fertility and magical essence. This mystical essence imbues the forest creatures, vegetation, and sometimes city dwellers, with potent magic. [[Dabnar Nevercough]], the esteemed Chief Magistrate, assumes the mantle of both head of state and Supreme Judge, governing over the realm of Stickyickistan. While [[Arcannabis]] stands as the city-state's primary export, considerable profits are also garnered from the trade and sale of Arcanite and other natural resources. Notably, since the arrival of human colonists, alcohol has been outlawed within the region due to its perceived threat to the Arcannabis market. Consequently, [[Zooka Malt]], a beverage derived from Arcannabis buds, has emerged as the main alternative to traditional ale, presenting a diverse array of Arcannabis-infused concoctions for the denizens to indulge in. Nevercough Island serves as a haven for high-end establishments, housing exclusive shops vending exquisite goods, a courthouse, a museum, a fine art gallery, and esteemed libraries, among other cultural landmarks.
16|
17|South of Nevercough Island, and north of the volcano, lies an area known as [[Lower South Booftown]], affectionately referred to as [[Booftown]]. This middle-class district paints a tranquil suburban picture with its small, family-owned shops and public parks. A constant flow of thick, dark, and slow-moving lava serves as a natural boundary, separating Lower South Booftown from its northern counterpart, aptly named [[Upper South Booftown]] or "[[The Ashtray]]" due to its gritty nature. The Ashtray harbors the city's darker underbelly and plays host to some of the realm's most notorious gangs. Among them, the MOB ([[Mandem on Booftown]]) and the CCC ([[Cough City Crew]]) dominate the landscape, engaging in relentless clashes over territorial disputes, control of illicit substances, weapons, arcane artifacts, and monetary gains. Upper South Booftown primarily houses the native Halfling population, alongside other minority groups. MOB remains an exclusively Halfling gang, while the CCC boasts a more diverse membership, encompassing various races, including Halflings, Humans, and other groups.
18|
19|To the east of the volcano lies Bobo Bush Estates, a realm where opulent mansions and lavish villas serve as the abodes for influential figures from Stickyickistan. North of Nevercough Island, the region of [[North Booftown]] thrives as the agricultural heartland of Stickyickistan. This area also harbors a Human criminal enterprise known as [[House Northbourne]], specializing in extortion, gambling, and the illicit distribution of bootleg alcohol. They cleverly employ a bookmaking business as a front for money laundering and maintain ownership of the North Booftown Downs, a renowned horse race track. The Norfies have faced accusations of engaging in illegal gambling and manipulating race outcomes. There is also a Dwarven settlement Dug into the base of Mount Zooka on the west side of the city called [[Bongstad]]. The Dwarves have cleverly engineered a magical geothermal power generation system that powers a majority of the [[Magitech]] grid in the realm. Some of the best forges on the island can be found in this part of town.
20|
21|Beyond the confines of the city lies what the residents of Stickyickistan call [[The Outback]], a colossal expanse of arcane forests, swamps, bogs, mountain ranges, jungle, rainforest, beaches, and a small area of badlands and desert at the southern end. The Outback is inhabited by creatures from all over the material plane and beyond. Due to the naturally high levels of pure magic spewed from Mount Zooka, the island has been a hotspot in the multiverse.
22|# Past Stickyickistan
23|
24|Stickyickistan didn't always have the tropical climate it has today. In the past the micro-climate of the island was in perfect balance of hot and cold areas, and arid and humid areas. The north part of the island had an ice cap, and the south was the similar to how it is now, but more like Mediterranean than Caribbean. The industrialization of the island has lead to massive climate change, and warming in the region which lead to the ice cap melting, and deserts replacing some old growth forests. There have been conservation efforts in recent times, but much of what used to be on the island has been lost.
25|## [[Human Colonialism]]
26|
27|In the annals of the multiverse, nestled amidst the turbulent seas, there exists an island now known as Stickyickistan. This extraordinary place, with its vibrant tapestry of cultures and bountiful resources, has a captivating history that intertwines the rise of its economy with the clash of two diverse civilizations.
28|
29|Long ago, the few, and only humanoid creatures on the island were a tranquil and harmonious community of halflings. They had a polytheistic faith in [[The Three Sisters]], lived in harmony with the land, and all the other creatures in it, cherishing the bountiful gifts bestowed upon them by the arcane nature of the island. The island flourished, its soil fertile and its forests teeming with life. But fate had other plans in store.
30|
31|In a wave of [[Human Colonialism]], ambitious settlers arrived upon the shores of Stickyickistan. Eager to claim the island's vast wealth for their own, they viewed the halflings as obstacles to their ambitions. Driven by greed and a desire to control the land's resources, the humans launched a forceful invasion, shattering the serenity that once enveloped the island. Forming the nation of Stickyickistan, and [[Nevercough City]] on what they now call [[Nevercough Island]]
32|
33|Amidst the chaos and conflict, the halflings valiantly resisted. Yet, outnumbered and outmatched, their hopes for victory dwindled. Recognizing the desperate situation, their wise leaders made a fateful decision—a negotiation for survival. A pact was struck, granting the halflings a protected enclave within the new nation now known as [[Upper South Booftown]], and acknowledging their rights to partake in the newfound prosperity.
34|
35|As the human settlers sought to establish dominion over the land, they discovered a remarkable resource—an extraordinary plant they called Arcannabis. Its magical properties became the foundation of Stickyickistan's economy, revolutionizing trade and transforming the island into a hub of prosperity. The potent properties of Arcannabis, when harnessed, granted individuals heightened senses, expanded magical abilities, and even visions into realms unseen.
36|
37|[[Arcannabis Cultivation]] quickly became a specialized art, passed down from generation to generation. Vast fields of the magical marijuana stretched across the landscape, tended to by expert cultivators who nurtured the plants with care and reverence. The nation's wealth soared as merchants flocked from distant lands to partake in the arcane wonders Stickyickistan had to offer.
38|
39|Underneath the bustling trade and enchanting haze, however, lay the remnants of a fractured society. The divide between the human settlers and the halfling community remained palpable, their coexistence marred by lingering distrust and cultural clashes. Nevertheless, as the economy thrived, the nation's leaders endeavored to bridge the gaps and foster unity among its diverse inhabitants.
40|
41|Over time, a unique blend of cultures emerged in Stickyickistan. The fusion of halfling traditions and human innovations birthed a captivating tapestry of art, music, and cuisine. Festivals celebrating both the halflings' reverence for nature and the humans' entrepreneurial spirit became the heartbeat of the city-state, uniting the population under a shared sense of identity. This is not to say that all racial tensions have gone away.
42|
43|Stickyickistan, with its majestic architecture, aromatic markets, and vibrant streets, stands today as a testament to the resilience and adaptability of its people. The island's history, forever marked by the invasion and subsequent coexistence, serves as a reminder of the complexities of cultural exchange and the potential for harmony amidst disparate communities.
44|
45|As the waves lap against the shores of Stickyickistan, the echoes of its past reverberate through the bustling city streets. The legacy of the halflings' ancestral connection to the land and the humans' quest for prosperity interweave to form the fabric of this remarkable island city-state, forever entwined with the enigmatic allure of Arcanite.
46|
47|## The Doobius House Resistance
48|
49|Stickyickistan wasn't always a city-state. It was once a nation with multiple population centers. The main [[Human]] settlement on [[Nevercough Island]] was named [[Nevercough City]] after its patriarchal noble family. A [[Dwarf]] settlement was excavated into the base of [[Mount Zooka]], across the [[Percolat Inlet]] from [[Nevercough City]], and named [[Bongstad]]. There was also a native [[Halfling]] reserved land, positioned between a giant lava river and the slopes of [[Mount Zooka]], where the terrain was barely habitable.
50|
51|Those settlements were all more or less on the coast of the nation, but one more settlement was established much farther inland: [[Doobius House]]. Founded by [[Duke Doobius Highblade]], it was intended to serve as the “Gate to the Outback”—a frontier town that attracted adventurers, prospectors, artificers, and others willing to live beyond the protection of the coastal settlements. At its height, Doobius House rivaled [[Nevercough City]] itself, producing towering arcane ballistae and nature-infused war machines.
52|
53|The town’s frontier purpose gave it an unusual character. Elyrian settlers, native Halflings, craftspeople, hunters, and exiles lived alongside one another, though not as equals. The Highblades claimed the land and profited from its workshops, while the Twothirdlings and other native communities supplied much of the local knowledge, labor, and military experience that kept the settlement alive.
54|
55|When [[Duke Doobius Highblade]] died, his human heirs inherited the family’s formal authority and attempted to preserve the old order. The Twothirdlings, who heavily outnumbered the Elyrian population around Doobius House, rejected that arrangement. Led by [[Jimmyjock Labingi]], the disinherited duke’s half-breed Twothirdling son, they seized the estate and surrounding settlement, declaring that Doobius House belonged to the people who had made it livable and defended it.
56|
57|Jimmyjock formed a provisional government and began negotiations with the Elyrian nobility of [[Nevercough City]]. The negotiations quickly broke down. The nobles refused to recognize the Twothirdlings’ claim to the settlement, while Jimmyjock refused to surrender the land or accept an arrangement that would leave his mother’s people subject to the family that had rejected him.
58|
59|## The [[Arcane Civil War]]
60|
61|The dispute over Doobius House became one of the first major armed conflicts between the Elyrian settlers and the native resistance. House Highblade forces attempted to retake the estate and secure the frontier road, while volunteers from Doobius House fortified the settlement and used the surrounding wilderness as a weapon.
62|
63|The resulting skirmishes spread into what is now known as the [[Grim Forest]]. Doobius House’s militia was badly outnumbered, but its fighters knew the terrain intimately. They used brutal guerrilla tactics, striking at night, cutting supply lines, sabotaging war machines, and disappearing into the forest before the larger Elyrian forces could respond. Old arcane ballistae, nature-infused war machines, trained beasts, and improvised traps allowed the resistance to ambush troops who expected a quick victory.
64|
65|The fighting around Doobius House became entangled with the wider power struggles among the [[Four Founding Houses]]. The houses disagreed over how quickly the frontier should be conquered, who would control its resources, and whether the Twothirdlings should be expelled, absorbed, or granted limited autonomy. Rival nobles supported, supplied, or undermined the campaign according to their own interests. House Highblade demanded a forceful restoration of its claim, while other factions used the conflict to weaken Highblade influence and seize control of the roads, workshops, and military technology produced at Doobius House.
66|
67|As the dispute widened, the conflict spread beyond the frontier. Industrial sabotage disrupted foundries and supply depots. Magical duels between noble arcanists devastated sections of the growing settlements. Factions summoned fiends, created unstable war golems, and unleashed necromantic plagues in attempts to gain the upper hand. The resulting violence made the original dispute over Doobius House only one front in a much larger struggle for control of the island’s government, resources, and future.
68|
69|The war was fought as much through espionage and sabotage as through open battle. Couriers disappeared along the frontier roads, military contracts changed hands through bribery, and entire workshops were destroyed rather than allowed to fall into an enemy faction’s control. The [[Grim Forest]] became a maze of abandoned siege engines, burned supply routes, hidden militia camps, and battlefields reclaimed by rapidly growing vegetation.
70|
71|The Twothirdling resistance did not cause the entire [[Arcane Civil War]], but it exposed the weakness of Elyrian rule. Doobius House became a symbol for both sides: to the resistance, proof that settlers could be defeated; to the nobles, proof that frontier autonomy threatened the authority of every ruling house. The conflict eventually widened into a prolonged civil war that reshaped the political order of the island.
72|
73|As the cost of the campaign mounted, the nobles of Nevercough City grew weary of trying to dominate a settlement that refused to surrender. The resistance had demonstrated that Doobius House could not be conquered cheaply, while continued warfare threatened trade routes and the stability of the coastal settlements. At the same time, the wider civil war forced the houses to redirect troops and resources away from the frontier.
74|
75|Jimmyjock used his knowledge of Elyrian law and military practice, combined with the indigenous values of his mother’s people, to negotiate a settlement. The final agreement recognized the Twothirdlings’ right to govern Doobius House, while allowing Elyrian families and institutions to remain in the region under negotiated protections. The settlement did not erase the violence or the unequal power that produced it, but it prevented House Highblade from reclaiming the town by force.
76|
77|Doobius House remained an autonomous and heavily armed frontier community for generations. Its workshops continued producing arcane ballistae and nature-infused war machines, officially for defense against the dangers of [[The Outback]], but also as a reminder that the town’s independence had been won through resistance. Jimmyjock’s songs preserved the memory of the conflict, while Elyrian histories recast him as a rebel and thief of noble property.
78|
79|In the aftermath of the [[Arcane Civil War]], the surviving settlements eventually united into the city-state of Stickyickistan. Doobius House lost much of its former independence as roads, bureaucracy, and urban expansion absorbed the frontier town into the wider state. Even so, the resistance remains central to its identity: the place where the Twothirdlings first proved that the Elyrian settlements could be challenged, and where Jimmyjock Labingi turned a disputed inheritance into a homeland.",

2|title: History of Stickyickistan
3|---
4|Stickyickistan is an island on the planet of [[Mythmos]] that is enshrouded in magic, and has one of the largest economies of all the realms. Their economy is based on the cultivation, and export of a wondrous magical plant called [[Arcannabis]], and . The size of the island and how far away it is from other land masses is mysterious at best. Even the most sophisticated magic and technology isn't capable of measuring distance within a certain distance of the island. This area is a Bermuda Triangle like place with its own micro-climate where pilots, and sailors have reported extreme magical weather events, and terrifying creatures from above and below. The presence of such large amounts of [[Arcanite]] beneath [[Mount Zooka]] has warped the fabric of time, space, and the weave itself around the island which is what causes these phenomenon. This makes it incredibly hard to produce a map of the whole island, as the coastlines are enigmatic at best. It can be seen from the [[Lumytholarispace]] , so it does appear on maps of Mythmos, but appears much smaller than going there would lead you to believe.
5|
6|

7|# Modern Stickyickistan
8|
9|Welcome to the enchanting realm of Stickyickistan, a City State where an active volcano stands proudly at its core. This bustling metropolis, inhabited by approximately 27 million denizens, thrives as a tightly woven tapestry of terraced dwellings. At the heart of it all lies the Capitol building, perched upon [[Nevercough Island]], an idyllic smaller landmass embraced by an inlet on the main island. The island experiences tropical weather patterns, with most days in the city being very hot and high in humidity. There are some arid areas of the island further inland where some levels of desertification have taken hold over the years after [[Human Colonialism]] and industrialization.
10|
11|Ascending from the base of the volcano, the upscale residences extend into the lush jungle, offering breathtaking vistas that stretch out to the majestic ocean. The colossal canopy of tropical trees, reminiscent of gargantuan redwoods, provides a natural shield, safeguarding inhabitants from the perilous potential of volcanic eruptions. In stark contrast, the slums that cling to the mountainside exude an aroma of brimstone and sulfur, perpetually shrouded in an ethereal haze of ash and smoke, reminiscent of the favelas of Brazil. These settlements wind their way upward, nearly reaching the rim of the crater in certain areas. Above the slums, an industrial district clings to the rim and delves deeper into the crater, thriving amidst the volcanic terrain.
12|
13|The centerpiece of this mesmerizing landscape, affectionately known to the locals as [[Mount Zooka]], is a unique marvel—a type of volcano called an [[Arcanite]] Cone. These particular cones rise above rich Arcanite deposits, their imposing forms resembling vast mounds of ebony volcanic rock. Near the base, dark, sluggish lava courses through the terrain, surrounding the volcano, while at its zenith, a massive crater brims with bubbling magma. During eruptions, projectiles ranging from golf ball-sized to soccer ball-sized volcanic rocks, globules of molten magma, and occasionally, chunks of Arcanite, burst forth from the crater. After each eruption, the valuable ores, minerals, and particularly the Arcanite, are harvested from the crater. Arcanite, a raw magical element typically found deep within the earth, can be extracted and purified, granting magical properties to weapons and armor. To facilitate this process, the government of Stickyickistan, aka the [[Nevercough Tribunal]], has established makeshift mines and outposts within and around the crater, providing shelter for workers during their resource-gathering shifts.
14|
15|The island's soil boasts copious amounts of nutrients, enriched by high traces of Arcanite. Consequently, the surrounding flora and fauna flourish with extraordinary fertility and magical essence. This mystical essence imbues the forest creatures, vegetation, and sometimes city dwellers, with potent magic. [[Dabnar Nevercough]], the esteemed Chief Magistrate, assumes the mantle of both head of state and Supreme Judge, governing over the realm of Stickyickistan. While [[Arcannabis]] stands as the city-state's primary export, considerable profits are also garnered from the trade and sale of Arcanite and other natural resources. Notably, since the arrival of human colonists, alcohol has been outlawed within the region due to its perceived threat to the Arcannabis market. Consequently, [[Zooka Malt]], a beverage derived from Arcannabis buds, has emerged as the main alternative to traditional ale, presenting a diverse array of Arcannabis-infused concoctions for the denizens to indulge in. Nevercough Island serves as a haven for high-end establishments, housing exclusive shops vending exquisite goods, a courthouse, a museum, a fine art gallery, and esteemed libraries, among other cultural landmarks.
16|
17|South of Nevercough Island, and north of the volcano, lies an area known as [[Lower South Booftown]], affectionately referred to as [[Booftown]]. This middle-class district paints a tranquil suburban picture with its small, family-owned shops and public parks. A constant flow of thick, dark, and slow-moving lava serves as a natural boundary, separating Lower South Booftown from its northern counterpart, aptly named [[Upper South Booftown]] or "[[The Ashtray]]" due to its gritty nature. The Ashtray harbors the city's darker underbelly and plays host to some of the realm's most notorious gangs. Among them, the MOB ([[Mandem on Booftown]]) and the CCC ([[Cough City Crew]]) dominate the landscape, engaging in relentless clashes over territorial disputes, control of illicit substances, weapons, arcane artifacts, and monetary gains. Upper South Booftown primarily houses the native Halfling population, alongside other minority groups. MOB remains an exclusively Halfling gang, while the CCC boasts a more diverse membership, encompassing various races, including Halflings, Humans, and other groups.
18|
19|To the east of the volcano lies Bobo Bush Estates, a realm where opulent mansions and lavish villas serve as the abodes for influential figures from Stickyickistan. North of Nevercough Island, the region of [[North Booftown]] thrives as the agricultural heartland of Stickyickistan. This area also harbors a Human criminal enterprise known as [[House Northbourne]], specializing in extortion, gambling, and the illicit distribution of bootleg alcohol. They cleverly employ a bookmaking business as a front for money laundering and maintain ownership of the North Booftown Downs, a renowned horse race track. The Norfies have faced accusations of engaging in illegal gambling and manipulating race outcomes. There is also a Dwarven settlement Dug into the base of Mount Zooka on the west side of the city called [[Bongstad]]. The Dwarves have cleverly engineered a magical geothermal power generation system that powers a majority of the [[Magitech]] grid in the realm. Some of the best forges on the island can be found in this part of town.
20|
21|Beyond the confines of the city lies what the residents of Stickyickistan call [[The Outback]], a colossal expanse of arcane forests, swamps, bogs, mountain ranges, jungle, rainforest, beaches, and a small area of badlands and desert at the southern end. The Outback is inhabited by creatures from all over the material plane and beyond. Due to the naturally high levels of pure magic spewed from Mount Zooka, the island has been a hotspot in the multiverse.
22|# Past Stickyickistan
23|
24|Stickyickistan didn't always have the tropical climate it has today. In the past the micro-climate of the island was in perfect balance of hot and cold areas, and arid and humid areas. The north part of the island had an ice cap, and the south was the similar to how it is now, but more like Mediterranean than Caribbean. The industrialization of the island has lead to massive climate change, and warming in the region which lead to the ice cap melting, and deserts replacing some old growth forests. There have been conservation efforts in recent times, but much of what used to be on the island has been lost.

title: History of Stickyickistan
---

Stickyickistan is an island on the planet of [[Mythmos]], shrouded in magic and home to one of the largest economies in the realms. Its wealth is built primarily on the cultivation and export of [[Arcannabis]], along with trade in [[Arcanite]] and other resources. The island’s size and distance from other landmasses are difficult to measure. Even the most sophisticated magic and technology fails beyond a certain distance from its shores.

The waters around Stickyickistan form a region much like a magical Bermuda Triangle. Pilots and sailors report violent weather, distorted horizons, impossible currents, and terrifying creatures from above and below. Vast deposits of [[Arcanite]] beneath [[Mount Zooka]] have warped time, space, and the Weave around the island, producing these phenomena and making accurate maps difficult to create. Stickyickistan can be seen from [[Lumytholarispace]] and appears on maps of Mythmos, but it always looks smaller than it seems when approached.

![[Stickyickistan.jpg]]

# Modern Stickyickistan

Stickyickistan is a city-state built around an active volcano. Approximately 27 million people live across its dense network of terraced districts. The Capitol stands on [[Nevercough Island]], a smaller landmass sheltered within an inlet on the main island. The climate is generally tropical, with hot, humid weather dominating the city. Farther inland, however, desertification has created increasingly arid regions, a legacy of [[Human Colonialism]] and industrialization.

Upscale residences climb from the volcano’s base into lush jungle, where they overlook the ocean. The immense canopy of trees, some resembling gigantic redwoods, provides a natural shield against volcanic eruptions. Below these elevated neighborhoods, settlements cling to the mountainside in a haze of ash, smoke, brimstone, and sulfur. Above them, an industrial district follows the crater’s rim and extends into the volcano itself.

The centerpiece of the city is [[Mount Zooka]], an [[Arcanite]] Cone. These volcanoes form above rich Arcanite deposits and rise as vast mounds of black volcanic rock. Dark, sluggish lava flows around the mountain’s base, while a crater filled with bubbling magma crowns its summit. Eruptions scatter volcanic stones, molten rock, and occasional chunks of Arcanite across the surrounding slopes. Afterward, workers harvest the valuable ores and minerals from the crater.

Arcanite is a raw magical element normally found deep underground. Once extracted and purified, it can grant magical properties to weapons and armor. The government, formally the [[Nevercough Tribunal]], maintains mines and outposts in and around the crater so workers have shelter during their shifts.

The island’s soil is rich in nutrients and infused with traces of Arcanite. As a result, its flora and fauna grow with extraordinary fertility and magical potency. This energy affects forest creatures, vegetation, and occasionally city dwellers. [[Dabnar Nevercough]], the Chief Magistrate, serves as both head of state and Supreme Judge. [[Arcannabis]] remains the city-state’s primary export, while Arcanite and other natural resources provide additional wealth.

Since the arrival of human colonists, alcohol has been outlawed because the government considers it a threat to the Arcannabis market. [[Zooka Malt]], a beverage made from Arcannabis buds, has become the principal alternative to traditional ale, with countless infused varieties sold throughout the city. [[Nevercough Island]] is home to the city-state’s most exclusive shops, courthouses, museums, galleries, libraries, and other cultural institutions.

South of Nevercough Island and north of the volcano lies [[Lower South Booftown]], commonly called [[Booftown]]. This middle-class district is known for family-owned shops and public parks. A slow-moving river of thick, dark lava separates it from [[Upper South Booftown]], also called [[The Ashtray]]. The Ashtray houses much of the city’s criminal underworld and is home to several notorious gangs. The MOB, or [[Mandem on Booftown]], and the CCC, or [[Cough City Crew]], compete for territory and control of illicit substances, weapons, arcane artifacts, and money.

Upper South Booftown is home primarily to the native Halfling population and other minority communities. The MOB remains exclusively Halfling, while the CCC includes Halflings, Humans, and members of other peoples.

To the east of the volcano lies [[Bobo Bush Estates]], a district of mansions and villas belonging to Stickyickistan’s wealthiest and most influential residents. North of Nevercough Island, [[North Booftown]] serves as the agricultural heartland. It is also home to [[House Northbourne]], a Human criminal enterprise specializing in extortion, gambling, and the illicit distribution of bootleg alcohol. The group uses a bookmaking business as a front for money laundering and owns the North Booftown Downs racetrack. The Norfies have been accused of fixing races and operating illegal gambling networks.

On the western side of the city, [[Bongstad]] is a Dwarven settlement carved into the base of Mount Zooka. Its engineers developed a magical geothermal power system that supplies much of the region’s [[Magitech]] grid. Bongstad is also known for producing some of the finest forges on the island.

Beyond the city lies [[The Outback]], a vast expanse of arcane forests, swamps, bogs, mountains, jungles, rainforests, beaches, badlands, and desert. Creatures from across the Material Plane and beyond inhabit the region. The pure magic released by Mount Zooka has made Stickyickistan a hotspot in the multiverse.

# Past Stickyickistan

Stickyickistan did not always have its current tropical climate. In earlier ages, the island maintained a more balanced pattern of hot and cold regions, as well as arid and humid zones. The northern part once held an ice cap, while the south resembled a Mediterranean climate more than a Caribbean one. Industrialization caused severe climate change. Rising temperatures melted the ice cap and turned some old-growth forests into desert. Recent conservation efforts have slowed the damage, but much of the original landscape has been lost.

## [[Human Colonialism]]

Long ago, the island’s only humanoid inhabitants were peaceful Halfling communities. They followed a polytheistic faith devoted to [[The Three Sisters]], lived in close relationship with the land, and respected the creatures that shared it. The island flourished, its soil was fertile, and its forests teemed with life.

That balance was disrupted when ambitious Human settlers arrived. Seeking control of the island’s resources, they treated the Halflings as obstacles and launched a violent invasion. The settlers established [[Nevercough City]] on what they called [[Nevercough Island]], forming the nation that would eventually become Stickyickistan.

The Halflings resisted, but they were outnumbered and outmatched. Their leaders eventually negotiated for survival. The resulting pact granted them a protected enclave in what is now [[Upper South Booftown]] and acknowledged their right to participate in the new nation’s prosperity.

The settlers later discovered [[Arcannabis]], an extraordinary plant whose magical properties became the foundation of the island’s economy. Properly cultivated, Arcannabis could heighten the senses, expand magical abilities, and reveal visions of unseen realms. [[Arcannabis Cultivation]] became a specialized tradition passed from generation to generation, and merchants soon traveled from distant lands to purchase the crop.

Economic prosperity did not erase the divisions created by colonization. Human settlers and Halfling communities continued to live with distrust, cultural conflict, and unequal access to power. Over time, their traditions and technologies blended into a distinctive culture of music, art, food, and festivals. This cultural exchange created a shared identity, but racial tensions never disappeared entirely.

Stickyickistan’s modern identity is therefore built on both coexistence and unresolved history. Its architecture, markets, and festivals reflect the fusion of Halfling traditions with Human innovation, while the island’s political institutions continue to bear the marks of conquest and resistance.

## The Doobius House Resistance

Stickyickistan was once a nation with several population centers rather than a single city-state. The main [[Human]] settlement on [[Nevercough Island]] was [[Nevercough City]], named for its patriarchal noble family. Across the [[Percolat Inlet]], [[Bongstad]] was carved into the base of [[Mount Zooka]]. The native [[Halfling]] reserve occupied land between a great lava river and the mountain’s slopes, where the terrain was barely habitable.

Farther inland, [[Doobius House]] was founded by [[Duke Doobius Highblade]] as the “Gate to the Outback.” The frontier settlement attracted adventurers, prospectors, artificers, and others willing to live beyond the protection of the coastal communities. At its height, Doobius House rivaled [[Nevercough City]] and became famous for producing arcane ballistae and nature-infused war machines.

Its frontier role gave Doobius House an unusual population. Elyrian settlers, native Halflings, craftspeople, hunters, and exiles lived beside one another, though not as equals. The Highblades claimed the land and profited from its workshops, while the Twothirdlings and other native communities supplied much of the local knowledge, labor, and military experience that kept the settlement alive.

When [[Duke Doobius Highblade]] died, his Human heirs inherited the family’s formal authority and attempted to preserve the old order. The [[Twothirdlings]], who heavily outnumbered the Elyrian population around Doobius House, rejected that arrangement. Led by [[Jimmyjock Labingi]], the duke’s disinherited Twothirdling son, they seized the estate and surrounding settlement. They declared that Doobius House belonged to the people who had made it livable and defended it.

Jimmyjock formed a provisional government and began negotiations with the Elyrian nobility of [[Nevercough City]]. The negotiations quickly failed. The nobles refused to recognize the Twothirdlings’ claim, while Jimmyjock refused to surrender the land or accept an arrangement that would leave his mother’s people subject to the family that had rejected him.

## The [[Arcane Civil War]]

The dispute over Doobius House became one of the first major armed conflicts between Elyrian settlers and the native resistance. House Highblade forces tried to retake the estate and secure the frontier road, while volunteers from Doobius House fortified the settlement and turned the surrounding wilderness into a weapon.

The resulting skirmishes spread into what is now called the [[Grim Forest]]. Doobius House’s militia was badly outnumbered, but its fighters knew the terrain intimately. They attacked at night, cut supply lines, sabotaged war machines, and disappeared into the forest before larger Elyrian forces could respond. Old arcane ballistae, nature-infused war machines, trained beasts, and improvised traps allowed the resistance to ambush troops who expected a quick victory.

The fighting around Doobius House became entangled with the wider power struggle among the [[Four Founding Houses]]. The houses disagreed over how quickly the frontier should be conquered, who would control its resources, and whether the Twothirdlings should be expelled, absorbed, or granted limited autonomy. Rival nobles supported, supplied, or undermined the campaign according to their own interests. House Highblade demanded that its claim be restored by force, while other factions used the conflict to weaken Highblade influence and seize the roads, workshops, and military technology produced at Doobius House.

As the dispute widened, the conflict spread beyond the frontier. Industrial sabotage disrupted foundries and supply depots. Magical duels between noble arcanists devastated sections of the growing settlements. Factions summoned fiends, created unstable war golems, and unleashed necromantic plagues in attempts to gain the upper hand. The original dispute over Doobius House became only one front in a larger struggle for control of the island’s government, resources, and future.

The war was fought through espionage and sabotage as much as open battle. Couriers disappeared along frontier roads, military contracts changed hands through bribery, and entire workshops were destroyed rather than allowed to fall into an enemy’s hands. The [[Grim Forest]] became a maze of abandoned siege engines, burned supply routes, hidden militia camps, and battlefields reclaimed by rapidly growing vegetation.

The Twothirdling resistance did not cause the entire [[Arcane Civil War]], but it exposed the weakness of Elyrian rule. Doobius House became a symbol for both sides. To the resistance, it proved that settlers could be defeated. To the nobles, it proved that frontier autonomy threatened the authority of every ruling house. The conflict widened into a prolonged civil war that reshaped the island’s political order.

As the cost of the campaign mounted, the nobles of Nevercough City grew weary of trying to dominate a settlement that refused to surrender. Doobius House could not be conquered cheaply, and continued warfare threatened trade routes and the stability of the coastal settlements. The wider civil war also forced the houses to redirect troops and resources away from the frontier.

Jimmyjock used his knowledge of Elyrian law and military practice, combined with the indigenous values of his mother’s people, to negotiate a settlement. The final agreement recognized the Twothirdlings’ right to govern Doobius House while allowing Elyrian families and institutions to remain under negotiated protections. The settlement did not erase the violence or the unequal power that produced it, but it prevented House Highblade from reclaiming the town by force.

Doobius House remained an autonomous and heavily armed frontier community for generations. Its workshops continued producing arcane ballistae and nature-infused war machines, officially to defend against the dangers of [[The Outback]], but also as a reminder that the town’s independence had been won through resistance. Jimmyjock’s songs preserved the memory of the conflict, while Elyrian histories recast him as a rebel and thief of noble property.

After the [[Arcane Civil War]], the surviving settlements eventually united into the city-state of Stickyickistan. Doobius House lost much of its former independence as roads, bureaucracy, and urban expansion absorbed the frontier town into the wider state. Even so, the resistance remains central to its identity. It was the place where the Twothirdlings first proved that Elyrian settlements could be challenged, and where Jimmyjock Labingi turned a disputed inheritance into a homeland.

North of Nevercough Island, [[North Booftown]] serves as the agricultural heartland. It is also home to [[House Northbourne]], a Human criminal enterprise specializing in extortion, gambling, and the illicit distribution of bootleg alcohol. The group uses a bookmaking business as a front for money laundering and owns the North Booftown Downs racetrack. The Norfies have been accused of fixing races and operating illegal gambling networks.

On the western side of the city, [[Bongstad]] is a Dwarven settlement carved into the base of Mount Zooka. Its engineers developed a magical geothermal power system that supplies much of the region’s [[Magitech]] grid. Bongstad is also known for producing some of the finest forges on the island.

Beyond the city lies [[The Outback]], a vast expanse of arcane forests, swamps, bogs, mountains, jungles, rainforests, beaches, badlands, and desert. Creatures from across the Material Plane and beyond inhabit the region. The pure magic released by Mount Zooka has made Stickyickistan a hotspot in the multiverse.

Stickyickistan did not always have its current tropical climate. In earlier ages, the island maintained a more balanced pattern of hot and cold regions, as well as arid and humid zones. The northern part once held an ice cap, while the south resembled a Mediterranean climate more than a Caribbean one. Industrialization caused severe climate change. Long ago, the island’s only humanoid inhabitants were peaceful Halfling communities. They followed a polytheistic faith devoted to [[The Three Sisters]], lived in close relationship with the land, and respected the creatures that shared it. Properly cultivated, Arcannabis could heighten the senses, expand magical abilities, and reveal visions of unseen realms. Economic prosperity did not erase the divisions created by colonization. Human settlers and Halfling communities continued to live with distrust, cultural conflict, and unequal access to power. Over time, their traditions and technologies blended into a distinctive culture of music, art, food, and festivals. This cultural exchange created a shared identity, but racial tensions never disappeared entirely.

Stickyickistan’s modern identity is therefore built on both coexistence and unresolved history. Its architecture, markets, and festivals reflect the fusion of Halfling traditions with Human innovation, while the island’s political institutions continue to bear the marks of conquest and resistance.

Stickyickistan was once a nation with several population centers rather than a single city-state. Farther inland, [[Doobius House]] was founded by [[Duke Doobius Highblade]] as the “Gate to the Outback.” The frontier settlement attracted adventurers, prospectors, artificers, and others willing to live beyond the protection of the coastal communities. At its height, Doobius House rivaled [[Nevercough City]] and became famous for producing arcane ballistae and nature-infused war machines.

Its frontier role gave Doobius House an unusual population. Elyrian settlers, native Halflings, craftspeople, hunters, and exiles lived beside one another, though not as equals. The Highblades claimed the land and profited from its workshops, while the Twothirdlings and other native communities supplied much of the local knowledge, labor, and military experience that kept the settlement alive.

When [[Duke Doobius Highblade]] died, his Human heirs inherited the family’s formal authority and attempted to preserve the old order. The [[Twothirdlings]], who heavily outnumbered the Elyrian population around Doobius House, rejected that arrangement. Led by [[Jimmyjock Labingi]], the duke’s disinherited Twothirdling son, they seized the estate and surrounding settlement. They declared that Doobius House belonged to the people who had made it livable and defended it.

Jimmyjock formed a provisional government and began negotiations with the Elyrian nobility of [[Nevercough City]]. The negotiations quickly failed. The nobles refused to recognize the Twothirdlings’ claim, while Jimmyjock refused to surrender the land or accept an arrangement that would leave his mother’s people subject to the family that had rejected him.

## The [[Arcane Civil War]]

The dispute over Doobius House became one of the first major armed conflicts between Elyrian settlers and the native resistance. House Highblade forces tried to retake the estate and secure the frontier road, while volunteers from Doobius House fortified the settlement and turned the surrounding wilderness into a weapon.

The resulting skirmishes spread into what is now called the [[Grim Forest]]. Doobius House’s militia was badly outnumbered, but its fighters knew the terrain intimately. They attacked at night, cut supply lines, sabotaged war machines, and disappeared into the forest before larger Elyrian forces could respond. Old arcane ballistae, nature-infused war machines, trained beasts, and improvised traps allowed the resistance to ambush troops who expected a quick victory.

The fighting around Doobius House became entangled with the wider power struggle among the [[Four Founding Houses]]. The houses disagreed over how quickly the frontier should be conquered, who would control its resources, and whether the Twothirdlings should be expelled, absorbed, or granted limited autonomy. Rival nobles supported, supplied, or undermined the campaign according to their own interests. House Highblade demanded that its claim be restored by force, while other factions used the conflict to weaken Highblade influence and seize the roads, workshops, and military technology produced at Doobius House.

As the dispute widened, the conflict spread beyond the frontier. Industrial sabotage disrupted foundries and supply depots. Magical duels between noble arcanists devastated sections of the growing settlements. Factions summoned fiends, created unstable war golems, and unleashed necromantic plagues in attempts to gain the upper hand. The original dispute over Doobius House became only one front in a larger struggle for control of the island’s government, resources, and future.

The war was fought through espionage and sabotage as much as open battle. Couriers disappeared along frontier roads, military contracts changed hands through bribery, and entire workshops were destroyed rather than allowed to fall into an enemy’s hands. The [[Grim Forest]] became a maze of abandoned siege engines, burned supply routes, hidden militia camps, and battlefields reclaimed by rapidly growing vegetation.

The Twothirdling resistance did not cause the entire [[Arcane Civil War]], but it exposed the weakness of Elyrian rule. Doobius House became a symbol for both sides. To the resistance, it proved that settlers could be defeated. To the nobles, it proved that frontier autonomy threatened the authority of every ruling house. The conflict widened into a prolonged civil war that reshaped the island’s political order.

As the cost of the campaign mounted, the nobles of Nevercough City grew weary of trying to dominate a settlement that refused to surrender. Doobius House could not be conquered cheaply, and continued warfare threatened trade routes and the stability of the coastal settlements. The wider civil war also forced the houses to redirect troops and resources away from the frontier.

Jimmyjock used his knowledge of Elyrian law and military practice, combined with the indigenous values of his mother’s people, to negotiate a settlement. The final agreement recognized the Twothirdlings’ right to govern Doobius House while allowing Elyrian families and institutions to remain under negotiated protections. The settlement did not erase the violence or the unequal power that produced it, but it prevented House Highblade from reclaiming the town by force.

Doobius House remained an autonomous and heavily armed frontier community for generations. Its workshops continued producing arcane ballistae and nature-infused war machines, officially to defend against the dangers of [[The Outback]], but also as a reminder that the town’s independence had been won through resistance. Jimmyjock’s songs preserved the memory of the conflict, while Elyrian histories recast him as a rebel and thief of noble property.

After the [[Arcane Civil War]], the surviving settlements eventually united into the city-state of Stickyickistan. Doobius House lost much of its former independence as roads, bureaucracy, and urban expansion absorbed the frontier town into the wider state. Even so, the resistance remains central to its identity. North of Nevercough Island, [[North Booftown]] serves as Stickyickistan’s agricultural heartland and the seat of [[House Northbourne]], the city-state’s least powerful noble house. Publicly, the Northbournes are respected breeders, handlers, and trainers of animals. They own [[The North Booftown Downs]], the premier horse-racing track, and founded the [[Handler’s Guild]], whose expertise extends from prized racehorses to exotic and magebred creatures. The family’s estate, surrounded by stables and pastures, is both their headquarters and a symbol of their influence.

In criminal circles, the Northbournes are informally called [[The Norfies]]. No member of Northbourne blood uses the name, since doing so can imply criminal affiliations and attract the attention of authorities such as the [[Nevercough Tribunal]] and the [[Tribunal Highblade Coalition]]. Behind the family’s respectable public image, the Norfies control Stickyickistan’s largest illicit [[Alcohol]] distribution network, manipulate racing odds and outcomes, operate high-stakes gambling syndicates, and host secret underground fighting rings. Their criminal operations are carried out through intermediaries, giving the noble family plausible deniability while preserving its control over North Booftown’s wealth and influence.

Upscale residences climb from the volcano’s base into lush jungle, where they overlook the ocean. The immense canopy of trees, some resembling gigantic redwoods, provides a natural shield against volcanic eruptions. Below these elevated neighborhoods, settlements cling to the mountainside in a haze of ash, smoke, brimstone, and sulfur. Above them, an industrial district follows the crater’s rim and extends into the volcano itself.

The centerpiece of the city is [[Mount Zooka]], an [[Arcanite]] Cone. These volcanoes form above rich Arcanite deposits and rise as vast mounds of black volcanic rock. Dark, sluggish lava flows around the mountain’s base, while a crater filled with bubbling magma crowns its summit. Eruptions scatter volcanic stones, molten rock, and occasional chunks of Arcanite across the surrounding slopes. Afterward, workers harvest the valuable ores and minerals from the crater.

Arcanite is a raw magical element normally found deep underground. Once extracted and purified, it can grant magical properties to weapons and armor. The government, formally the [[Nevercough Tribunal]], maintains mines and outposts in and around the crater so workers have shelter during their shifts.

The island’s soil is rich in nutrients and infused with traces of Arcanite. As a result, its flora and fauna grow with extraordinary fertility and magical potency. This energy affects forest creatures, vegetation, and occasionally city dwellers. [[Dabnar Nevercough]], the Chief Magistrate, serves as both head of state and Supreme Judge. [[Arcannabis]] remains the city-state’s primary export, while Arcanite and other natural resources provide additional wealth.

Since the arrival of human colonists, alcohol has been outlawed because the government considers it a threat to the Arcannabis market. [[Zooka Malt]], a beverage made from Arcannabis buds, has become the principal alternative to traditional ale, with countless infused varieties sold throughout the city. [[Nevercough Island]] is home to the city-state’s most exclusive shops, courthouses, museums, galleries, libraries, and other cultural institutions.

South of Nevercough Island and north of the volcano lies [[Lower South Booftown]], commonly called [[Booftown]]. This middle-class district is known for family-owned shops and public parks. A slow-moving river of thick, dark lava separates it from [[Upper South Booftown]], also called [[The Ashtray]]. The Ashtray houses much of the city’s criminal underworld and is home to several notorious gangs. The MOB, or [[Mandem on Booftown]], and the CCC, or [[Cough City Crew]], compete for territory and control of illicit substances, weapons, arcane artifacts, and money.

Upper South Booftown is home primarily to the native Halfling population and other minority communities. The MOB remains exclusively Halfling, while the CCC includes Halflings, Humans, and members of other peoples.

To the east of the volcano lies [[Bobo Bush Estates]], a district of mansions and villas belonging to Stickyickistan’s wealthiest and most influential residents. North of Nevercough Island, [[North Booftown]] serves as Stickyickistan’s agricultural heartland and the seat of [[House Northbourne]], the city-state’s least powerful noble house. Publicly, the Northbournes are respected breeders, handlers, and trainers of animals. They own [[The North Booftown Downs]], the premier horse-racing track, and founded the [[Handler’s Guild]], whose expertise extends from prized racehorses to exotic and magebred creatures. The family’s estate, surrounded by stables and pastures, is both their headquarters and a symbol of their influence.

In criminal circles, the Northbournes are informally called [[The Norfies]]. No member of Northbourne blood uses the name, since doing so can imply criminal affiliations and attract the attention of authorities such as the [[Nevercough Tribunal]] and the [[Tribunal Highblade Coalition]]. Behind the family’s respectable public image, the Norfies control Stickyickistan’s largest illicit [[Alcohol]] distribution network, manipulate racing odds and outcomes, operate high-stakes gambling syndicates, and host secret underground fighting rings. Their criminal operations are carried out through intermediaries, giving the noble family plausible deniability while preserving its control over North Booftown’s wealth and influence.

On the western side of the city, [[Bongstad]] is a Dwarven settlement carved into the base of Mount Zooka. Its engineers developed a magical geothermal power system that supplies much of the region’s [[Magitech]] grid. Bongstad is also known for producing some of the finest forges on the island.

Beyond the city lies [[The Outback]], a vast expanse of arcane forests, swamps, bogs, mountains, jungles, rainforests, beaches, badlands, and desert. Creatures from across the Material Plane and beyond inhabit the region. The pure magic released by Mount Zooka has made Stickyickistan a hotspot in the multiverse.

2|
3|An underground metropolis that is a part of the city of [[Stickyickistan]], but it is the underbelly of the city where [[The Mortuary]] is located, and where the [[Dungsweepers]] toil. Home to many undesirables, the elites of the city above mostly ignore the happenings of this under city. the under city has it's own provisional government, but holds no authority in the eyes of the Nevercough Tribunal.
4|
5|The Nevercough Tribunal refuses to acknowledge Osslurraggath, but every noble knows their waste doesn’t vanish by magic — it _goes somewhere._
6|
7|- When Stickyickistan grew into a great metropolis, the [[Nevercough Tribunal]] needed a place for the poor, the diseased, and the dishonored dead. They built vast **bone vaults** beneath the city to serve as its necropolis.
8|- These vaults eventually collapsed into deeper Underdark channels. What should have been a tomb became a **threshold**, spilling with refuse, plague-bodies, and exiles.
9|- Into this void stepped the **[[Heralds of Dust]]** — led by **[[Factol Skall]]**. They declared that all life in Stickyickistan was already death, and that Osslurraggath would be the sanctum where this truth was embraced.
10|The name Osslurraggath comes from the common word "Ossuary", and the Drow word "lurraggath" meaning love.

      "content": "1|Doobius House is a village in [[The Outback]] of [[Stickyickistan]] inhabited by indigenous [[Twothirdlings]], and a few full Halflings. This village was founded in the earliest years of [[Human Colonialism]] and is named after the head of [[House Highblade]], and a great military leader of old, [[Duke Doobius Highblade]]. A thriving village in its hay day, it boasted the highest population of any inland settlement. In the current day, it is a run-down village with a very similar population to what it had in its prime. The growth of the town stagnated once the frontier, and native populations had been conquered / assimilated and there was no longer a need for a major inland post.
2|
3|# History
4|
5|During it's hay day the town had a bustling economy relative to the time. Many adventurers would pass through the village streets, and although it is nothing like the city of Stickyickistan today, the village had plenty of options for commerce.
6|
7|# POIs
8|
9|### Hotbox Inn & Tavern
10|
11|Owner: [[Barnabas Huggins]]
12|
13|Players can rest here, and buy food, drink, and novice level [[Arcannabis]] strains from Barnabas. Barnabas also may have some info about happenings around the town. He can not make Arcannabis strains he just sells it.
14|
15|**Barnabas Huggins** is a stout, rosy-cheeked man in his mid-50s, with thinning auburn hair combed stubbornly across his head and a laugh that seems to roll out of his belly like a thunderclap. He dresses in plain but well-kept clothes, his apron always dusted with flour or ale stains. Barnabas is a natural storyteller—half of what he says is truth, the other half is so exaggerated that even he forgets where the line is. He has a warm, booming hospitality, but he also has a sharp eye; nothing that happens under his roof escapes his notice. Regulars know him as a man who can get you anything—whether it’s a good smoke, a hot meal, or a whispered rumor—provided you’ve got coin and keep out of trouble.
16|
17|Voice & Mannerisms
18|- Loud, booming laugh that fills the room.
19|- Talks in long-winded stories, often blending truth with exaggeration.
20|- Always wiping his apron with a rag, though it never seems clean.
21|- Winks knowingly when sharing a rumor or deal.
22|Attitude
23|- Warm, welcoming, and larger-than-life.
24|- Sharp-eyed despite his jolly demeanor—nothing slips past him.
25|- Pragmatic: willing to deal in food, drink, smoke, and gossip if coin’s on the table.
26|- Protective of his inn’s peace—rowdiness is tolerated, but troublemakers get the boot.
27|Interactions
28|- Greets newcomers like old friends, drawing them into tales of “what really happened” years ago.
29|- Sells food, drink, and novice-level Arcannabis strains, but insists he’s “no grower, just a seller.”
30|- Slips rumors or local news into casual conversation, often for the price of a pint.
31|- Knows how to balance being everyone’s friend with being the quiet watcher of the room.
32|
33|### Burial Barrow
34|
35|This is an ancient burial place that the pioneers of the village have appropriated as their own.
36|
37|### Celestial Chapel
38|
39|This is a special church built by the clergy specifically for training new missionaries, and "converting" natives. Not where the common folk go to pray.
40|
41|### [[Grim Forest]] Edge
42|
43|The origins of the grim forest are not known. The only knowledge of this place is held by indigenous elders that haven't lost their oral history traditions. Evil plants, and some undead roam this forest. The edge of the woods is guarded by an ancient awakened radiant tree.
44|
45|### Village Greengrocer
46|
47|Owner: [[Matilda "Tilly" Cabbagewhistle]]
48|
49|Tilly is a sprightly halfling woman in her late 60s, though she insists she’s “still young enough to outrun a carrot thief.” She’s got wiry gray hair tied back in a messy bun, sharp green eyes, and hands stained from years of pulling weeds and weighing apples. She’s endlessly chatty—every purchase comes with at least two local rumors and three unsolicited cooking tips. Beneath her cheerful demeanor, she’s fiercely protective of her stall and her produce, wielding her broom with alarming speed when would-be thieves try their luck.
50|
51|Voice & Mannerisms
52|- Fast-talking, cheerful, always has a story or rumor to share.
53|- Sharp green eyes that miss very little.
54|- Waves her hands when speaking, often holding a vegetable for emphasis.
55|- Keeps a broom nearby and isn’t shy about brandishing it.
56|Attitude
57|- Energetic and sprightly despite her age.
58|- Fiercely protective of her produce and her stall.
59|- Warm and neighborly, though a little nosy.
60|- Prideful about freshness and quality—takes offense at haggling.
61|Interactions
62|- Every sale comes with gossip, cooking advice, or both.
63|- Treats regular customers like family, but expects respect.
64|- Chases thieves with broom in hand—swift and merciless in defense of her goods.
65|- Has a soft spot for children, often slipping them fruit for free.
66|
67|### Town Square
68|
69|In the center of the town square there is a Fountain of holy water that is blessed by priests daily and dawn and dusk. Both human and halfling commoners will come here to pray. The fountain is surrounded by stone brick buildings, and an elevated concourse leading to a some local businesses. These businesses include:
70|
71| - Butcher
72| - florist
73| - tailor
74| - guard post
75| - bookshop
76|
77|### Hidden "Witch" Hut
78|
79|NPC: [[Thalion Mossgrove]]

      "content": "1|
2|**Molten Maw** is a colossal underground volcanic city in the [[Underdark]], inhabited mainly by [[Duergar]] and [[Svirfneblin]]. Built around a vast open caldera beneath the earth, the city serves as both a natural forge and a deadly hazard. Its streets are carved into black basalt terraces, iron gantries, cooled lava shelves, and tunnels reinforced against constant tremors.
3|
4|Rivers of semi-intelligent, magically charged lava course through the city’s depths. Locals call these flows **the Veins**, and treat them less like ordinary magma and more like dangerous spirits of the earth. The lava sometimes changes course without warning, answers certain forms of elemental magic, or rises into half-formed elemental creatures that guard the flows from thieves, miners, and careless outsiders.
5|
6|## Character
7|
8|Molten Maw is brutal, smoky, rich, and paranoid. Every surface is warm. Every shadow glows faintly red. The air tastes of metal, ash, and old bargains. Duergar foundries hammer day and night, while Svirfneblin engineers maintain hidden vents, cooling chambers, pressure gates, and secret escape tunnels.
9|
10|The city is famous for:
11|
12|- Infernal heat and volcanic hazards
13|- Masterwork metal, obsidian, glass, and gemstone craft
14|- Hidden smuggler dens
15|- Elemental lava cults
16|- Political exiles and escaped criminals
17|- The underground black market known as [[The Silt Road]]
18|
19|## The Silt Road
20|
21|Criminals, rebels, fugitives, and desperate surface-folk sometimes flee to Molten Maw, surviving in fire-resistant cave networks and hidden market warrens. Over time, these routes became the heart of [[The Silt Road]], a literal underground criminal market that moves contraband, people, secrets, cursed goods, monster parts, and forbidden magic beneath the notice of surface authorities.
22|
23|The Silt Road does not truly belong to any one faction. Duergar clans tax it, Svirfneblin guides navigate it, smugglers profit from it, and local gangs bleed for control of it.
24|
25|## Notable Features
26|
27|- **The Veins:** Semi-intelligent lava rivers that move through the city like living arteries.
28|- **The Chain Terraces:** Stacked residential districts connected by chains, lifts, bridges, and mine platforms.
29|- **The Cinder Warrens:** Smuggler caves, fugitive dens, and black-market stalls hidden behind cooling vents.
30|- **The Glass Forges:** Workshops where volcanic glass, enchanted slag, and fire-tempered gems are shaped.
31|- **The Ash Courts:** Harsh civic chambers where Duergar clan leaders, Svirfneblin engineers, and criminal brokers negotiate.
32|- **The Mouth Below:** A deeper volcanic pit believed to be either a planar wound, sleeping primordial, or the source of the Veins.
33|
34|## Dangers
35|
36|- Sudden lava surges
37|- Toxic gas pockets
38|- Collapsing tunnels
39|- Elemental guardians
40|- Duergar press gangs
41|- Svirfneblin sabotage traps
42|- Criminal ambushes
43|- Heat exhaustion
44|- Deals that are harder to escape than the city itself
45|
46|## Adventure Hooks
47|
48|- A fugitive the party needs has vanished into the Cinder Warrens.
49|- A shipment moving along [[The Silt Road]] contains something far worse than contraband.
50|- One of the Veins has begun spelling warnings in molten stone.
51|- A Duergar clan hires the party to recover a stolen forge-secret recipe.
52|- A Svirfneblin engineer believes the Mouth Below is waking up.
53|- Surface rebels want weapons from Molten Maw, but buying them may empower the wrong faction.",

      "content": "1|Looming over [[Stickyickistan]], the colossal Mount Zooka is an active [[Arcanite]] Cone—a rare type of volcano that sits atop rich Arcanite deposits, constantly pulsing with magical energy. Its obsidian-black slopes, laced with glowing veins of molten rock, serve as both a natural wonder and a relentless hazard. While its slow-moving lava flows encircle the base, its violent eruptions hurl flaming debris, molten magma, and even raw chunks of Arcanite across the land.
2|
3|The mountain is a center of industry and danger, with miners, [[Magitech]] engineers, and reckless bounty hunters carving out makeshift tunnels and outposts along its rim, seeking precious minerals, arcane artifacts, and volatile magical energy. The [[Bongstad]] dwarves have built their fortified settlement into the base of the mountain, using its natural heat to power their forges. Meanwhile, the upper crater is home to industrial mining operations, dangerous alchemical experiments, and the ruins of those who dug too deep.
4|
5|Mount Zooka is the heart of Stickyickistan’s power and chaos—a force of creation and destruction, where great fortunes and terrible disasters are only ever one eruption away.
6|
7|Mount Zooka's indigenous name is - Wachii Zookaamihk - which roughly translates to - Mountain Place of Sacred Stones.",

      "content": "1|# Springwood
2|
3|**Springwood** is a massive naturalized park in the heart of [[Stickyickistan]], an ancient sacred woodland so revered that even the [[Human Colonialism|Elyrian settlers]] hesitated to defile it. The forest has always existed in a state of impossible spring: bright leaves, blooming flowers, soft rain, birdsong, and warm green air no matter the season beyond its borders.
4|
5|The woodland is broad and temperate, dominated by old deciduous trees and dotted with small human, halfling, and gnomish settlements. [[Kerning’s Crossing]] sits along the main trade road, known for its apothecaries and its dependence on the nearby [[Solarium Botanica]]. When the Botanica thrives, merchants, alchemists, herbalists, and Arcannabis growers prosper. When its resources dry up, whole storefronts shutter within days.
6|
7|Recently, Springwood has begun changing faster than anyone can explain. Creatures fleeing the Plane of Fey have carried strange seeds into the forest, and those seeds are taking root with alarming speed. Glittering fairies flit through the canopy, perfumes drift on the wind and cloud mortal judgment, and songs echo between the trees at night. Rainbow lights shimmer across ponds and streams, luring travelers off the path and deeper into a forest that feels less like a park each day and more like a hungry dream.
8|
9|# Regional Effects 
10|
11|Exposure to the faerie realm has begun to affect the area surrounding the Solarium Botanica, creating one or more of the following effects: 
12|
13|***Feymagic Storms.*** Isolated micro storms of fey magic randomly occur within the 6-mile area surrounding the glasshouse. Instead of rain and lightning, these micro storms create time dilations and illusions that last 1 hour in one of the following d4 ways: 
14|
15|1. Plants bloom, fruit, wither, and bud again, as if the seasons were rapidly accelerated. 
16|2. The sun seems to creep barely above the horizon, putting the area in perpetual twilight. 
17|3. The perception of non-fey creatures in the area are warped, causing extreme bouts of giddiness and happy hallucinations.
18|4. Winter takes hold of the area, and plants wither under a coating of frost and ice. 
19|	- ***Faerie Rings.*** Strange mushroom rings grow haphazardly over the region within 6 miles of the glasshouse. Whenever a living creature steps into one, it is teleported to a random location on the Plane of Fey for 1 hour before returning to the same place 1d4 hours later. The time dilation is very confusing.
20|	- ***Overgrowth.*** New plants have proliferated throughout the forest, shifting the landscape drastically. These changes include overgrown roads and paths that are now unnavigable, forcing travelers to take new paths never walked before
21|
22|# Unique Flora & Fauna 
23|
24|Although the Springwood has always been home to some fey creatures, like blink squirrels, the recent influx of creatures (and the seeds they spread) is changing the fauna and flora of this unique biosphere. Here are a few examples of the more remarkable changes the characters may encounter during their journey through the forest: 
25|
26|#### ***Honeyvine.*** 
27|Honeyvine is an epiphytic plant that grows along the trunks and branches of trees. It is a deep golden colour and exudes a sweet, honey-like sap with an irresistible smell. Those who touch the vine or taste its sap are quickly trapped by the sticky substance, unable to move (or talk, if it is tasted), as the fluid begins to digest its victims alive. Honeyvine releases a burst of sticky sap in a 5-foot radius around itself whenever a living creature touches it. Each creature in the area must succeed on a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw or become restrained in the sap. A restrained creature takes 7 (2d6) acid damage at the start of each of its turns. A creature can use an action to make a DC 13 Strength (Athletics) check, freeing itself or a restrained creature within its reach on a success. 
28|
29|#### ***Glowshrooms.*** 
30|The glowshroom is a small, luminescent fey plant found in shadowy undergrowth. They grow in clusters on the ground or the sides of trees and have a soft, sponge-like texture. Eating a glowshroom causes the creature’s skin and hair to cast a dim, bioluminescent light out to 5 feet for 1 hour. A creature can’t become invisible while under the effects of a glowshroom, and creatures that can see the glowing creature have advantage on attack rolls against it. A creature that eats more than one glowshroom in a 24-hour period becomes poisoned until it next finishes a long rest. 
31|
32|#### ***Lyrefly.*** 
33|The lyrefly is a fey insect that resembles a butterfly with a four-inch wingspan and shimmering, colourful body. It is known for its beautiful wings, which resemble the strings of a lyre, and its ability to produce sweet, melodic music as it flutters through the trees. Despite its charming appearance, the carnivorous lyrefly is also a formidable hunter. A swarm of lyreflies (see Appendix C) can turn their music into thunder effects to stun and disorient their prey.",

      "content": "1|Beyond the sprawling cityscape of [[Stickyickistan]] lies The Outback, a vast and untamed and largely unexplored wilderness of many biomes where civilization fades and nature takes hold. A dense, tangled expanse of towering [[Arcanite]]-infused trees, hidden rivers, and ancient ruins, it is a land of hermits, cults, and creatures from all over the multiverse.
2|
3|The Outback is home to those who reject city life, whether by choice or necessity. Exiled criminals, rogue druids, and forgotten warlocks carve out lives in the wild, while strange communes and doomsday cults worship the land’s raw, untapped magic. The deeper one ventures, the more dangerous it becomes—feral beasts, wandering spirits, and ancient arcane anomalies lurk beyond the jungle’s edge, waiting for foolish trespassers.
